 Follow Ryan Reynolds Turns Avengers: Doomsday Credits Buzz Into a Deadpool Punchline
 Nitish Singh Thu, November 12, 2026 at 9:16 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Credits: Marvel Studios Ryan Reynolds has responded to the latest Avengers: Doomsday casting speculation with a joke only Deadpool could deliver. After a post on X highlighted writing credits listing Reynolds and Hugh Jackman as contributors to the Marvel film, the actor shared a short clip from his movie that turned the discussion into a punchline.
 The post displayed the two actors under the film's "Additional Literary Material" credits. Reynolds responded with a 3.5-second clip featuring Deadpool saying, "Oh, there's no need for paperwork," followed by, "Good! Not to brag, but I do not read." 
 The latest developments add to the growing excitement around Avengers: Doomsday
 The Writers Guild of America listing names Reynolds and Jackman alongside several other contributors, including Eric Pearson, Chris McKenna, Erik Sommers, Jeff Loveness, Andrew Lanham, and Destin Daniel Cretton. Stephen McFeely and Michael Waldron hold the film's main writing credits.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The listing has fueled speculation that the two actors could appear in Avengers: Doomsday. However, writing credits alone do not confirm that either will reprise their Marvel roles. Reynolds and Jackman have also joked about joining the film during appearances at San Diego Comic-Con and D23, but Marvel has yet to officially announce their involvement.
 Other developments have added to the anticipation. The VisionQuest finale featured a post-credits scene revealing Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch, with Doctor Doom appearing to have plans for her powers. The film is also expected to bring together characters from the Avengers, Fantastic Four, Thunderbolts, and X-Men franchises.
 Robert Downey Jr. leads the story as Doctor Doom, while Chris Evans and Chris Hemsworth are among the returning MCU stars. The cast also includes several actors from the original Fox X-Men films, including Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Rebecca Romijn, and Kelsey Grammer.
 Joe and Anthony Russo are directing the crossover, which is scheduled to arrive in theaters on December 18, 2026. Until Marvel confirms the full lineup, Reynolds' Deadpool joke has given fans another entertaining clue to discuss, even if it does not settle the casting question.
